item.content:encoded:
Organizations, artists, cultural practitioners, and social change leaders in Oakland now have an opportunity to secure long-term funding through the Belonging in Oakland: A Just City Cultural Fund 2026. The initiative is accepting applications for its fourth annual funding round, offering substantial financial support to collaborative partnerships working toward racial equity, social justice, and community transformation.

The program recognizes that meaningful social change happens when artists, culture bearers, organizers, and nonprofit organizations collaborate to address systemic issues affecting their communities. Rather than funding artistic work in isolation, the initiative encourages partnerships that combine creativity with civic engagement, policy advocacy, and community organizing.

Through this funding opportunity, selected collaborations will receive $100,000 annually for three consecutive years, creating a total funding package of $300,000 per collaboration. In addition, participating artists and cultural practitioners will receive annual living stipends and funding dedicated to documenting their work.

This initiative represents one of Oakland’s most significant investments in the intersection of arts, culture, and social justice.

About Belonging in Oakland: A Just City Cultural Fund

Belonging in Oakland: A Just City Cultural Fund is a collaborative funding initiative designed to strengthen partnerships between artists and organizations committed to creating a more equitable and inclusive Oakland.

The program is supported through a partnership involving:

  • East Bay Community Foundation (EBCF)
  • Akonadi Foundation
  • City of Oakland Cultural Affairs Division

The initiative also receives major financial support from the Surdna Foundation’s Thriving Cultures Program.

Since its establishment in 2020, the Fund has invested in projects that use arts and culture as powerful tools to address systemic inequality, amplify marginalized voices, and inspire policy and community transformation.

The underlying philosophy of the Fund is that culture is not separate from civic life—it is an essential driver of social change.

Grant Value and Funding Benefits

Successful collaborations will receive an extensive package of financial support designed to sustain long-term impact.

The funding includes:

  • $100,000 each year
  • Funding period of three years
  • Total grant value of $300,000 per selected collaboration
  • $12,000 annual living stipend for participating artists and cultural practitioners
  • $25,000 allocated specifically for documenting the collaboration
  • Long-term support for community-centered cultural projects
  • Resources to strengthen partnerships between artists and organizers
  • Support for initiatives promoting racial justice and community belonging
  • Increased visibility for funded collaborations
  • Opportunity to influence civic systems, policies, and community narratives

The funding structure allows organizations to move beyond short-term projects and instead build sustainable collaborations capable of producing lasting community impact.

Purpose of the Fund

The Fund seeks projects that move beyond traditional artistic programming by combining creative expression with social justice work.

Applicants are encouraged to develop projects that:

  • Challenge harmful racial narratives
  • Promote racial equity
  • Create inclusive civic participation
  • Strengthen community leadership
  • Build equitable partnerships
  • Develop new community structures
  • Encourage shared decision-making
  • Inspire policy change
  • Foster belonging among historically marginalized communities
  • Create lasting systems of justice and inclusion

Rather than funding isolated events, the Fund prioritizes initiatives capable of producing meaningful structural and cultural transformation.

History and Previous Funding Rounds

Since launching in 2020, the Belonging in Oakland initiative has supported numerous innovative collaborations.

First Round (2020)

The inaugural funding round responded to the COVID-19 pandemic by supporting artists who helped communities imagine a more equitable Oakland during a time of crisis.

Projects encouraged residents to rethink public life, civic participation, and social justice during unprecedented challenges.

Second Round (2021)

The second funding cycle expanded the program by supporting two-year collaborative projects focused on:

  • Combating systemic racism
  • Elevating marginalized voices
  • Challenging structural inequities
  • Promoting community-led change

Third Round (2023)

The most recent round funded collaborations that addressed critical community issues, including:

  • Supporting immigrants who were formerly or currently incarcerated
  • Advancing equitable development in Oakland Chinatown
  • Strengthening Black cultural spaces throughout Oakland

These initiatives demonstrated how partnerships between artists and community organizations can reshape public dialogue while influencing policies affecting local communities.

Who Can Apply?

The Fund is specifically designed for collaborative partnerships.

Eligible lead applicants must be:

  • Cultural organizations working with artists and cultural practitioners, or
  • Social change organizations collaborating with artists and culture bearers.

The lead organization must satisfy all eligibility requirements established by the Fund.

Eligibility Requirements

Applicants must meet the following conditions.

Organizational Requirements

Lead applicants must:

  • Hold IRS-recognized 501(c)(3) status, or
  • Hold IRS-recognized 501(c)(4) status, or
  • Have an eligible 501(c)(3) fiscal sponsor in good standing.

In addition, applicants should:

  • Be based in Oakland
  • Serve BIPOC communities
  • Demonstrate experience in community engagement
  • Show evidence of successful partnerships
  • Have an operating budget of at least $500,000

What Types of Projects Are Encouraged?

The Fund welcomes innovative collaborations that:

  • Address racial inequities
  • Support community healing
  • Build civic participation
  • Promote social justice
  • Develop new models of community leadership
  • Shift harmful public narratives
  • Increase equity through arts and culture
  • Encourage collaboration across sectors
  • Strengthen neighborhoods
  • Expand opportunities for historically marginalized communities

Projects should demonstrate mutual benefit between artists and organizational partners while contributing toward a more just Oakland.

Application Process

The application process consists of two stages.

Step 1: Submit a Letter of Interest (LOI)

Eligible applicants must submit:

  • Letter of Interest
  • Organizational information
  • Financial statements for the most recently completed fiscal year
  • Work samples demonstrating policy change or community impact

Step 2: Invitation to Submit Full Proposal

After reviewing Letters of Interest, the Fund will invite up to 10 applicants to submit comprehensive proposals.

Only shortlisted organizations will advance to the second stage.

Application Timeline

Applicants should carefully observe the following important dates.

Activity Date
Applications Open July 2026
How-to-Apply Webinar August 12, 2026 (11:00 a.m.–1:00 p.m. PT)
Letter of Interest Deadline August 28, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. PT
Awards Announced Late October 2026

Late or incomplete applications will not be considered.

Required Documents

Applicants should prepare:

  • Letter of Interest
  • Organizational profile
  • Financial records
  • Recent fiscal information
  • Policy change work samples
  • Partnership information
  • Supporting documentation requested by the Fund

Webinar for Prospective Applicants

To help applicants understand the funding opportunity, organizers will host an informational webinar.

The webinar will cover:

  • Eligibility requirements
  • Application process
  • Required documents
  • Selection criteria
  • Frequently asked questions
  • Tips for preparing a competitive application

Attendance is strongly encouraged for all prospective applicants.

To register for the Webinar on how to apply visit HERE

Why This Grant Matters

Many grant programs provide funding only for short-term activities. In contrast, Belonging in Oakland offers multi-year investment, enabling organizations and artists to build lasting partnerships.

The program recognizes that cultural practitioners play an essential role in:

  • Influencing public dialogue
  • Building trust
  • Promoting healing
  • Advancing racial justice
  • Inspiring civic participation
  • Supporting community resilience
  • Transforming public systems

By combining financial support with documentation resources and artist stipends, the initiative creates an environment where collaborations can thrive over several years.

Visit HERE to learn more about the Belonging in Oakland

Organizations Behind the Initiative

The Belonging in Oakland: A Just City Cultural Fund is made possible through collaboration among respected philanthropic and public institutions.

These include:

  • East Bay Community Foundation
  • Akonadi Foundation
  • City of Oakland Cultural Affairs Division
  • Surdna Foundation’s Thriving Cultures Program

Together, these organizations seek to strengthen Oakland by investing in arts, culture, racial equity, and community leadership.

Deadline

Letter of Interest (LOI) Deadline: Friday, August 28, 2026, at 5:00 p.m. Pacific Time (PT).

Late or incomplete submissions will not be accepted.

Conclusion

The Belonging in Oakland: A Just City Cultural Fund 2026 represents an exceptional opportunity for Oakland-based cultural organizations, artists, and social change leaders committed to building a more equitable future. By offering $300,000 in funding over three years, alongside artist stipends and documentation support, the initiative provides the resources needed to create meaningful, community-driven change. Organizations with a proven commitment to racial equity, civic engagement, and collaborative leadership are encouraged to prepare strong applications before the August 28, 2026 deadline. This funding is more than a grant—it is an investment in creative partnerships that have the power to transform communities, reshape public narratives, and build a more just Oakland for future generations.

item.content:encoded:
The Dresden Leibniz Graduate School (DLGS) has officially opened applications for its 2027 International PhD Programme, offering fully funded doctoral scholarships for outstanding graduates interested in advancing research on sustainable urban mobility transformations. The programme seeks innovative researchers capable of addressing some of the world’s most pressing urban mobility and sustainability challenges through interdisciplinary and transformative research.

Successful applicants will receive a full-time scholarship for three years, including a monthly stipend of €1,515, together with financial support for research activities and travel. Hosted jointly by the Leibniz Institute of Ecological Urban and Regional Development (IOER) and TU Dresden (Dresden University of Technology), the programme provides an outstanding research environment focused on spatial sustainability science and transformative leadership.

About the Dresden Leibniz Graduate School (DLGS)

The Dresden Leibniz Graduate School (DLGS) is an interdisciplinary graduate school jointly operated by the Leibniz Institute of Ecological Urban and Regional Development (IOER) and TU Dresden.

The graduate school is dedicated to advancing research in:

  • Spatial Sustainability Science
  • Ecological Urban Development
  • Urban and Regional Planning
  • Sustainable Transformation
  • Transformative Leadership
  • Interdisciplinary Research

Its doctoral programme encourages collaboration across disciplines to generate practical solutions for global sustainability challenges while preparing researchers for leadership roles in academia, government, and industry.

Theme of the 2027 Call

Levers for Sustainable Urban Mobility Transformations

The 2027 call focuses on identifying innovative solutions capable of transforming urban mobility systems into more sustainable, inclusive, efficient, and resilient systems.

According to DLGS, modern urban mobility systems face numerous structural sustainability challenges, including:

  • Heavy dependence on fossil fuels
  • Environmental pollution
  • Negative public health impacts
  • Accessibility inequalities
  • Social inequity
  • Road safety concerns
  • Fragmented planning systems
  • Poor integration between transport planning and land-use development

While digitalization, automation, electrification, artificial intelligence, and new mobility services are transforming transportation systems at unprecedented speed, they also introduce new complexities and unintended consequences.

The programme therefore seeks doctoral research capable of addressing these challenges through integrated and interdisciplinary approaches.

Why This Research Matters

Urban mobility is no longer viewed solely as transportation.

Instead, it has become closely connected with:

  • Urban planning
  • Environmental sustainability
  • Climate action
  • Economic development
  • Digital innovation
  • Public governance
  • Social inclusion
  • Technological transformation

Current planning approaches often separate transport systems from land-use planning despite their strong interdependence. Existing business models also remain dominated by traditional transport providers, while innovative mobility solutions frequently remain confined to niche applications.

The emergence of spatial data science, artificial intelligence, advanced modelling, and digital technologies presents significant opportunities to rethink how cities are planned and managed.

DLGS therefore encourages research capable of integrating these dimensions into comprehensive mobility transformation strategies.

Key Research Gaps Identified by DLGS

The programme highlights several major research gaps that applicants are encouraged to address.

These include:

1. Integration of Spatial and Mobility Systems

Research is needed to better understand how spatial planning and mobility interact across different geographical scales and contexts.

2. Advanced Models for Dynamic Mobility Systems

Applicants are encouraged to develop models capable of analysing:

  • Normal transport operations
  • Disrupted mobility systems
  • Effects of automation
  • Effects of digitalization
  • Decision-support systems for planners

3. Combining Data Science with Public Participation

The programme seeks approaches that merge:

  • Data-driven analytics
  • Participatory planning
  • Co-creation
  • Inclusive decision-making

4. Future Scenario Development

Researchers should explore mobility futures ranging from:

  • Real-time scenarios
  • Short-term planning
  • Medium-term transitions
  • Long-term sustainable futures

while accounting for uncertainty.

5. Governance and Institutional Innovation

The role of institutions, governance systems, and business models in enabling or limiting sustainable mobility transformations remains an important research area.

6. Inclusion of Vulnerable Groups

Projects should consider how mobility systems can better serve vulnerable populations through inclusive design and evaluation.

7. Interdisciplinary Integration

DLGS also identifies insufficient collaboration between disciplines such as:

  • Transport research
  • Spatial planning
  • Spatial data science
  • Urban informatics

The programme seeks research that bridges these fields.

Research Topics

Applicants should develop doctoral projects addressing at least one of the following challenge-driven topics.

1. Public Policy

Possible research areas include:

  • Governance structures
  • Institutional design
  • Planning instruments
  • Policy implementation
  • Planning techniques

2. Business Models

Potential research themes include:

  • Sustainable mobility businesses
  • Private-sector innovation
  • Civil society solutions
  • Third-sector organizations
  • Non-profit service delivery
  • Economic sustainability

3. Integrative Tools

Projects may focus on:

  • Data-driven approaches
  • Analytical methods
  • Computational models
  • Decision-support interfaces
  • Digital tools

4. Integrated Perspectives

Applicants may also develop interdisciplinary concepts connecting:

  • Public policy
  • Private sector
  • Civil society
  • Third-sector organizations

through shared methods, practices, and collaborative frameworks.

Applicant Profile

DLGS is looking for outstanding graduates with strong academic backgrounds and a clear research vision.

Applicants should demonstrate:

  • Academic excellence
  • Strong analytical skills
  • Innovative thinking
  • Interest in sustainability research
  • Interdisciplinary collaboration
  • Commitment to solving complex urban challenges

Eligibility Requirements

Applicants must satisfy all of the following requirements:

  • Hold a Master’s degree in a relevant discipline.
  • Have obtained their first Master’s degree within the previous three years.
  • Demonstrate above-average academic performance.
  • Submit an original research proposal aligned with DLGS research priorities.
  • Identify potential supervisors at TU Dresden and/or IOER.
  • Submit all required application materials before the deadline.

For projects connected to ongoing IOER activities in the Dresden/Saxony region, applicants must also demonstrate German language proficiency at C1 level.

Expectations for the Research Proposal

Applicants are expected to prepare an original doctoral proposal reflecting both their academic expertise and research interests.

Projects may use:

  • Qualitative research
  • Quantitative research
  • Empirical analysis
  • Computational modelling
  • Conceptual research
  • Methodological innovation

Interdisciplinary approaches are expected, while transdisciplinary research designs involving broader stakeholder collaboration are explicitly encouraged whenever feasible.

Scholarship Benefits

Successful candidates will receive:

  • Full-time PhD scholarship.
  • Funding for three years.
  • Monthly scholarship of €1,515.
  • Additional financial support for:
    • Research activities
    • Academic travel

The programme also provides access to an internationally recognized interdisciplinary research environment through DLGS, IOER, and TU Dresden.

Programme Timeline

Activity Date
Application Deadline September 1, 2026
Programme Start March 1, 2027

How to Apply

Interested applicants should prepare all required application materials and submit them through the official online application system before the deadline.

Applicants are encouraged to carefully review the detailed application requirements and procedures available on the DLGS website before submitting their applications.

APPLY HERE

Contact Information

For additional information regarding the programme, applicants may contact:

Scientific Coordinator

Dr. Nora Gortcheva

Email: dlgs@ioer.de

Visit HERE to learn more about the DLGS Call for Applications 2027

Application Deadline

September 1, 2026

Conclusion

The DLGS International PhD Programme 2027 presents an exceptional opportunity for talented graduates seeking to contribute to the future of sustainable urban mobility through cutting-edge interdisciplinary research. By bringing together expertise from transport studies, spatial planning, data science, governance, economics, and related fields, the programme aims to generate innovative solutions to some of the world’s most pressing urban sustainability challenges. With a fully funded three-year scholarship, a competitive monthly stipend, additional research and travel support, and access to internationally recognized research institutions, the programme provides an outstanding platform for aspiring researchers committed to shaping more inclusive, resilient, and sustainable cities. Prospective applicants are encouraged to prepare a strong research proposal aligned with the programme’s priorities and submit their applications before the September 1, 2026 deadline.

For more global schorlarship opportunities visit OFY HERE

item.content:encoded:
Applications are now open for the prestigious New York Times Local Investigations Fellowship 2027–2028, a unique opportunity for local journalists and freelance reporters to spend an entire year pursuing an ambitious investigative reporting project with mentorship from some of the most respected investigative journalists in the world.

The fellowship is designed to support journalists who have identified important local accountability stories but lack the time, resources, editorial support, or investigative capacity to fully pursue them. Selected fellows will work under the guidance of Dean Baquet, former Executive Editor of The New York Times, alongside a team of veteran investigative editors while producing impactful journalism that will be edited and published by The New York Times.

The programme provides participants with the rare opportunity to sharpen their investigative reporting skills, receive expert editorial guidance, and produce work that can create meaningful change in their communities.

Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, and the deadline is 21 August 2026.

 

About The New York Times

The New York Times is one of the world’s most respected news organizations. Its mission is to seek the truth and help people understand the world through independent, high-quality journalism. The organization maintains a globally recognized newsroom with journalists reporting from nearly 160 countries and remains committed to producing impactful journalism across print, digital, audio, and multimedia platforms.

The Local Investigations Fellowship was established to help talented reporters investigate significant local stories that deserve deeper reporting and greater accountability.

Selected fellows will remain based within their communities while conducting investigative reporting focused on their state, city, or region. Fellows will also make periodic visits to New York Times offices for training, mentorship, and editorial support.

The fellowship emphasizes accountability journalism that uncovers important truths, reveals hidden issues, and highlights matters affecting people’s lives, safety, livelihoods, and wellbeing.

Throughout the programme, fellows will receive direct mentorship from experienced investigative editors while learning advanced investigative techniques, editorial judgment, and reporting strategies.

 

Fellowship Benefits

Selected fellows will receive:

  •  A full year dedicated to investigative reporting.
  •  Mentorship from Dean Baquet and veteran investigative editors.
  • Editorial guidance from The New York Times newsroom.
  • Professional training and investigative journalism support.
  • Publication opportunities through The New York Times.
  • Access to experienced investigative journalism professionals.
  • Opportunities to strengthen reporting, sourcing, and storytelling skills.
  • Exposure to one of the world’s leading journalism organizations.
  •  Competitive annual compensation of $85,262.84.

Additional employment benefits may include medical, dental, vision, retirement benefits, paid leave, tuition reimbursement, and professional development support.

 

Responsibilities of Fellows

Selected fellows will:

  •  Spend one year producing high-impact investigative journalism.
  •  Focus on accountability reporting within their state or region.
  •  Develop and execute an original investigative project.
  • Work closely with experienced editors.
  •  Conduct in-depth research and source development.
  •  Produce reporting that meets New York Times standards.
  •  Demonstrate commitment to journalistic independence.
  • Contribute meaningful stories that help communities understand important issues.

 

Eligibility Criteria

Applicants must meet the following requirements:

Required Qualifications

  • Three to five years of professional reporting experience.
  •  Experience covering a specific beat for a local newspaper or digital news outlet.
  • Be an independent journalist or employed by a newsroom willing to grant a year-long sabbatical.
  •  Authorization to work in the United States. The fellowship does not sponsor new work visas
  • Applicants are encouraged to demonstrate:

 

Preferred Qualifications 

  • Significant experience covering local issues.
  • A strong investigative story idea that requires additional resources and editorial support.
  • Ability to bring fresh perspectives to investigative journalism.
  • Commitment to accountability reporting and community-centered journalism.

 

What Makes a Strong Application?

The fellowship seeks applicants with compelling local investigative ideas that:

Address High-Stakes Issues

The story should impact people’s lives, health, safety, livelihoods, or quality of life.

Establish Accountability

Strong investigations focus on institutions, organizations, or individuals with significant power and influence.

Reveal New Information

The proposed investigation should uncover information that has not yet been fully exposed.

Demonstrate Need

The strongest applications clearly explain why the issue is important to a specific community and why it deserves investigation.

 

Application Requirements

Applicants must submit:

  • Resume

An updated professional résumé.

  • Cover  Letter

The cover letter must include at least one investigative story idea or pitch. Applicants may submit multiple story ideas if desired.

Each story idea should address:

  • The investigative focus.
  • What new information the investigation may reveal.
  • Who has been harmed and how.
  • Who may be held accountable.
  • Required records, data, and sources.
  • Reporting barriers and needed support.
  • Existing reporting on the topic.

Five Published Clips

Applicants must submit five published clips demonstrating excellence in journalism, impactful reporting, and community-centered storytelling. Full text versions should be included .

Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis.

Applicants are encouraged to apply as early as possible.

 

Why You Should Apply

The New York Times Local Investigations Fellowship is one of the most exciting opportunities available to local journalists in the United States. Few programmes offer the chance to spend an entire year pursuing a major investigative project with the mentorship of award-winning editors while having your work published by one of the world’s most influential news organizations.

For journalists who are passionate about accountability reporting and uncovering stories that matter, this fellowship provides unmatched resources, guidance, and professional development opportunities.

Apply Here

Apply through The New York Times careers portal before 21 August 2026.

Conclusion

The New York Times Local Investigations Fellowship 2027–2028 offers an extraordinary opportunity for local journalists and freelancers to pursue impactful investigative reporting with support from some of the best editors in the industry. Through a year of focused reporting, mentorship, and professional development, fellows will gain the skills, resources, and editorial guidance needed to produce journalism that can drive accountability and create meaningful change. If you have a powerful local story that deserves national attention, this fellowship could provide the platform and support needed to bring it to light.

Discover more fellowship opportunities like this HERE .

item.content:encoded:
Journalists and aspiring movement reporters seeking to deepen their reporting skills while contributing meaningful stories about social justice movements have an exceptional opportunity through the Waging Nonviolence Fellowship 2026. This prestigious five-month journalism fellowship is designed for writers who are passionate about covering movements for peace, democracy, racial justice, labor rights, environmental justice, and other forms of nonviolent social change. Unlike many journalism programs that focus on general news reporting, the Waging Nonviolence Fellowship provides specialized editorial mentorship, practical reporting experience, and financial support while allowing fellows to build an impressive portfolio of published work. Participants work closely with experienced editors, produce in-depth feature stories, and become part of a respected publication known internationally for its coverage of grassroots movements and civil resistance.

The fellowship is fully remote for applicants based in the United States, offering participants the flexibility to manage their own schedules while receiving professional editorial guidance from seasoned journalism professionals.

About the Waging Nonviolence Fellowship

The Waging Nonviolence Fellowship is a professional journalism training program that combines mentorship, reporting, writing, and publishing opportunities over a five-month period. Rather than functioning as a traditional classroom program, the fellowship provides real-world editorial experience where participants actively report on undercovered movement issues and publish long-form feature articles on the Waging Nonviolence platform. Throughout the fellowship, participants strengthen their investigative reporting, interviewing, storytelling, research, and feature writing skills while contributing meaningful journalism that reaches activists, scholars, organizers, policymakers, and readers around the world. The fellowship particularly focuses on reporting stories that often receive little attention from mainstream media, helping fellows develop expertise in movement journalism and solutions-oriented reporting.

What Fellows Will Do

Successful applicants will spend five months working closely with the editorial team while producing original journalism.

During the fellowship, each participant will:

  • Write five original feature articles.
  • Publish one feature article each month.
  • Produce articles with a minimum length of 1,500 words.
  • Pitch original story ideas.
  • Conduct interviews and research.
  • Report on social movements and grassroots organizing.
  • Receive editorial feedback throughout the writing process.
  • Develop stronger investigative journalism skills.
  • Build a professional portfolio of published work.

This hands-on structure allows fellows to gain valuable publishing experience while refining every stage of the reporting process.

Fellowship Benefits

The Waging Nonviolence Fellowship offers numerous professional and financial benefits that can significantly advance a journalist’s career.

1. Financial Support

Participants receive compensation throughout the fellowship.

Financial benefits include:

  • An initial stipend of $500 upon joining the program.
  • $250 for every published feature story.

Since each fellow publishes five stories during the fellowship, participants receive compensation while building an impressive portfolio of professional journalism.

2. Personalized Editorial Mentorship

One of the fellowship’s greatest strengths is direct mentorship from experienced editors.

Participants work closely with:

  • Senior Editor Jessica Stites.
  • Editor-in-Chief Eric Stoner.

Editors help fellows improve:

  • Story development.
  • Pitch writing.
  • Reporting techniques.
  • Interview strategies.
  • Feature writing.
  • Narrative structure.
  • Editing skills.
  • Investigative journalism practices.

The mentorship begins with an introductory meeting and continues throughout the fellowship whenever additional editorial guidance is needed.

3. Flexible Remote Work

The fellowship is conducted entirely online.

Participants benefit from:

  • Remote work.
  • Flexible scheduling.
  • Self-directed workflow.
  • Independent reporting opportunities.
  • Freedom to organize their own writing schedule.

This flexibility allows fellows to balance the fellowship alongside other professional commitments while maintaining editorial deadlines.

4. Opportunity to Build a Strong Journalism Portfolio

Every published feature becomes part of the fellow’s professional writing portfolio.

Publishing multiple long-form investigative stories demonstrates:

  • Reporting experience.
  • Research ability.
  • Interviewing skills.
  • Editorial collaboration.
  • Long-form writing expertise.
  • Subject matter specialization.

A strong portfolio can significantly improve future career opportunities within journalism and media.

5. Exposure to Influential Audiences

Waging Nonviolence is widely respected among:

  • Movement organizers.
  • Human rights advocates.
  • Activists.
  • Researchers.
  • Policy professionals.
  • Academics.
  • Civil society organizations.
  • Independent journalists.

Publishing on the platform allows fellows to reach readers interested in meaningful social change rather than producing click-driven content.

Career Opportunities After the Fellowship

The fellowship has helped launch the careers of numerous journalists.

Former writers have gone on to contribute to respected media organizations, including:

  • Democracy Now!
  • Vox
  • The Guardian
  • The Intercept
  • The New Republic
  • Rolling Stone

The fellowship therefore serves as a valuable stepping stone for journalists seeking careers in investigative reporting, movement journalism, and public interest media.

Fellowship Requirements

Applicants should possess strong journalism skills and a demonstrated interest in covering social movements.

Required qualifications include:

  • Experience reporting on social movements.
  • Experience producing reported analysis.
  • Excellent writing ability.
  • Ability to submit polished, publication-ready articles.
  • Passion for movements promoting peace and justice.
  • Ability to work independently.
  • Strong communication skills.
  • Reliability in meeting deadlines.
  • Responsiveness to editorial communication.

Preferred Qualifications

Although not mandatory, applicants with the following experience may be particularly competitive:

  • Existing relationships with activist organizations.
  • Connections with grassroots communities.
  • Experience covering racial justice movements.
  • Experience reporting on labor organizing.
  • Familiarity with democracy defense initiatives.
  • Knowledge of civil resistance.
  • Understanding of nonviolent action strategies.
  • Knowledge of movement history and organizing tactics.

Work Expectations

Throughout the fellowship, participants are expected to:

  • Independently identify compelling story ideas.
  • Conduct in-depth reporting.
  • Meet agreed deadlines.
  • Communicate regularly with editors.
  • Respond promptly to editorial feedback.
  • Produce accurate, engaging, and thoroughly researched feature stories.

The fellowship emphasizes initiative, professionalism, and high-quality journalism.

Commitment to Diversity and Inclusion

Waging Nonviolence strongly believes that journalism benefits from diverse perspectives.

The organization welcomes applicants from all backgrounds and particularly encourages applications from individuals belonging to communities that have historically been underrepresented within the media industry.

This commitment reflects the publication’s broader mission of amplifying voices that are often overlooked in mainstream journalism.

About Waging Nonviolence

item.content:encoded:
Applications are now open for the Perspective Fund Documentary Film Support 2026, an opportunity designed to support documentary filmmakers and narrative strategists who are closest to the issues their films address and are uniquely positioned to create meaningful social impact.

The Perspective Fund invests in documentary projects that have the potential to expand public understanding, shape culture, strengthen movements, and contribute to systems change. Rather than supporting films solely for artistic merit, the fund prioritizes projects that can influence public discourse, advance advocacy efforts, and create lasting societal impact.

The program recognizes the power of storytelling as a tool for change and seeks filmmakers whose work can contribute something distinct and valuable to ongoing efforts in journalism, advocacy, movement building, and public life.

For documentary filmmakers seeking support to advance impactful storytelling, the Perspective Fund offers an important opportunity to receive funding and strategic backing.

 

About the Perspective Fund

The Perspective Fund supports documentary filmmakers and narrative strategists whose projects address critical social, political, environmental, cultural, and economic issues.

The fund focuses on stories that can:

  •  Expand public understanding.
  • Influence culture and public dialogue.
  • Strengthen social movements.
  • Advance advocacy efforts.
  • Drive systems-level change.
  • Support public-interest storytelling.

Unlike traditional film grants that primarily evaluate artistic production, the Perspective Fund places strong emphasis on impact, community accountability, strategic clarity, and issue expertise.

 

What Types of Projects Does the Perspective Fund Support?

The Perspective Fund seeks projects that go beyond raising awareness and actively contribute to meaningful change.

Successful projects often demonstrate the ability to:

  • Address pressing social issues.
  • Advance public understanding of complex challenges.
  • Strengthen existing movements and advocacy efforts.
  • Shift public narratives.
  • Influence decision-makers.
  • Promote accountability.
  • Build community engagement.
  • Contribute to long-term systems change.

Projects can focus on a wide range of issues, including:

  •  Human rights
  • Social justice
  • Climate and environmental issues
  • Democracy and governance
  • Economic inequality
  • Public health
  • Education
  • Migration
  • Community development
  • Civic participation

 

What the Perspective Fund Looks For

The Perspective Fund evaluates applicants across multiple dimensions to identify projects with the greatest potential for impact.

1. Strategic Clarity

Applicants should demonstrate a clear understanding of:

  •  What they are creating.
  • Why the project matters.
  • Who the project serves.
  • The change the project aims to achieve.

Strong projects have a well-defined vision and strategy for impact.

2. Community Accountability and Power

The fund prioritizes filmmakers who maintain authentic relationships with the communities represented in their work.

Projects should demonstrate:

  •  Ethical storytelling practices.
  • Community engagement.
  • Respect for participants and stakeholders.
  • Accountability to affected communities.

 3. Issue Expertise and Landscape Awareness

Applicants should show a deep understanding of the issue they are addressing.

This includes:

  • Knowledge of existing efforts.
  • Understanding of relevant stakeholders.
  • Awareness of policy, advocacy, and movement landscapes.
  • Familiarity with current narratives surrounding the issue.

4. Narrative Impact

The Perspective Fund seeks stories capable of shifting perspectives and influencing public conversations.

Projects should have the potential to:

  • Reach key audiences.
  • Challenge existing assumptions.
  • Introduce new perspectives.
  • Generate meaningful dialogue.

 5. Contribution to Broader Change

Projects should demonstrate how the documentary can support broader efforts already underway within movements, journalism, advocacy, or public life.

The strongest applications clearly explain how storytelling will contribute to existing change-making efforts.

 

Why Apply?

Documentary filmmaking plays a critical role in informing the public, amplifying underrepresented voices, and shaping social change.

The Perspective Fund offers filmmakers an opportunity to:

  • Secure funding for impactful projects.
  • Advance strategic storytelling efforts.
  • Increase the reach and influence of their work.
  • Build stronger connections with advocacy and movement partners.
  • Create documentaries that contribute to lasting societal change.
  • Strengthen narrative strategies around important issues.

For filmmakers working on stories that matter, this support can help transform ideas into meaningful action.

 

Application Process

Interested applicants should complete the official inquiry form and provide information about:

  •  Their documentary project.
  • Intended impact goals.
  • Community engagement approach.
  • Issue expertise.
  • Strategic vision.
  • Storytelling objectives.

Applicants are encouraged to clearly demonstrate both creative excellence and impact potential.

 

Who Should Apply?

This opportunity is ideal for:

  • Documentary filmmakers.
  • Investigative storytellers.
  • Independent filmmakers.
  • Narrative strategists.
  • Impact producers.
  • Journalism-focused filmmakers.
  • Advocacy storytellers.
  • Media professionals working on social change project

Application Link
Log onto this portal to apply.

Conclusion

The Perspective Fund Documentary Film Support 2026 offers a valuable opportunity for documentary filmmakers and narrative strategists seeking to create impactful stories that contribute to public understanding and social change. By supporting projects that strengthen movements, shape culture, and drive systems-level impact, the fund empowers storytellers to create work that matters. Filmmakers with compelling documentary projects focused on meaningful change are encouraged to submit an inquiry and explore this funding opportunity.

Discover more grants opportunities like this HERE

item.content:encoded:
Entrepreneurs building innovative solutions for biodiversity conservation and sustainable environmental impact now have an exciting opportunity to accelerate the growth of their startups through the Brainforest Venture Program 2026. Designed specifically for ambitious early-stage ventures, this intensive 10-week accelerator provides founders with hands-on coaching, personalized mentorship, expert guidance, investor exposure, and the opportunity to receive a $125,000 investment in exchange for equity. The program brings together entrepreneurs, investors, conservation experts, and industry leaders to help startups develop scalable businesses that generate both financial returns and measurable environmental impact. Whether your startup focuses on forest conservation, ecosystem restoration, biodiversity protection, climate resilience, sustainable agriculture, or nature-positive technologies, the Brainforest Venture Program offers the resources and ecosystem needed to transform promising ideas into investment-ready ventures.

With applicants accepted from around the world, this global program supports startups whose solutions can make a meaningful difference in biodiversity hotspots and environmentally threatened regions.

About the Brainforest Venture Program

The Brainforest Venture Program is a specialized startup accelerator that focuses exclusively on ventures creating positive outcomes for forests, biodiversity, and ecosystems. Unlike traditional startup accelerators that prioritize rapid financial growth alone, Brainforest seeks founders whose businesses integrate environmental impact into the heart of their business model.

The accelerator combines:

  • Intensive venture coaching
  • Individual mentoring
  • Investment readiness preparation
  • Business model refinement
  • Expert-led learning sessions
  • Networking opportunities
  • Access to impact investors
  • Long-term ecosystem support

Throughout the ten-week program, participants work closely with experienced venture builders who help strengthen every aspect of their business, from strategy and operations to fundraising and investor communications.

Why Biodiversity Startups Matter

The world faces unprecedented environmental challenges, including:

  • Deforestation
  • Habitat destruction
  • Species extinction
  • Climate change
  • Soil degradation
  • Water scarcity
  • Ecosystem collapse

Innovative businesses have an important role to play in addressing these challenges. Brainforest believes startups can develop scalable solutions that generate both commercial success and lasting environmental benefits.

The Venture Program is therefore designed for founders who understand that business growth and ecological restoration can go hand in hand.

What Participants Can Expect

Participants receive comprehensive support throughout the program.

1. Dedicated One-on-One Coaching

Each startup is assigned a dedicated venture coach who works closely with the founding team throughout the program.

The coach helps participants:

  • Define clear objectives
  • Identify priorities
  • Improve strategic planning
  • Validate business assumptions
  • Refine market positioning
  • Develop investment strategies
  • Solve operational challenges
  • Generate actionable insights

This personalized support ensures founders receive tailored advice specific to their venture’s needs.

2. Access to Industry Experts and Mentors

Beyond individual coaching, startups engage with experienced professionals from multiple industries.

Participants gain access to:

  • Biodiversity experts
  • Conservation specialists
  • Startup founders
  • Business strategists
  • Investment professionals
  • Technical advisors
  • Sustainability leaders
  • Domain experts

These mentors share practical knowledge and real-world experience to help founders overcome challenges and accelerate growth.

3. Financial Support

One of the most attractive aspects of the Brainforest Venture Program is the opportunity for selected ventures to receive:

$125,000 investment in exchange for equity.

This funding enables startups to:

  • Scale operations
  • Expand teams
  • Improve products
  • Enter new markets
  • Prepare for future fundraising rounds
  • Accelerate business growth

4. Access to an Extensive Global Network

Brainforest has built a strong international network over many years working in biodiversity and forest conservation.

Participants gain access to:

  • Non-governmental organizations (NGOs)
  • Impact investors
  • Venture capital professionals
  • Unicorn founders
  • Environmental organizations
  • Corporate partners
  • Fellow entrepreneurs
  • Global conservation community

Networking opportunities often continue long after the program concludes.

Who Should Apply?

The program targets startups that already have an initial foundation and are ready to grow.

Ideal applicants include ventures that meet the following criteria:

Early-Stage Companies

Applicants should be at:

  • Pre-seed stage
  • Seed stage

The startup should already have:

  • A working product
  • A prototype
  • A pilot project
  • Initial validation

Committed Founding Teams

Brainforest expects founders to dedicate themselves fully throughout the ten-week accelerator.

Applicants should be prepared to:

  • Attend coaching sessions
  • Participate in workshops
  • Meet mentors
  • Engage with investors
  • Continuously improve their business

Global Startups

The program welcomes applications from companies headquartered anywhere in the world.

Rather than focusing on company location, Brainforest prioritizes ventures whose solutions can operate in:

  • Biodiversity hotspots
  • Forest regions
  • Areas facing ecosystem degradation
  • Nature-threatened environments

Businesses That Combine Profit and Impact

Applicants should demonstrate that:

  • Biodiversity is central to the business model.
  • Revenue and environmental impact grow together.
  • Business success directly contributes to healthier ecosystems.
  • Sustainability is integrated into the company’s long-term strategy.

Program Timeline

The Brainforest Venture Program follows a structured journey that helps founders steadily improve their businesses.

1. Application Window

25 July 2026 – 17 August 2026

Applicants should prepare:

  • Updated pitch deck
  • Business documents
  • Company information
  • Application form

2. Selection Period

17 August 2026 – 15 September 2026

During this stage:

  • Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis.
  • Shortlisted startups are invited for interviews.
  • Final participants are selected.

3. Team Onboarding

28 September – 2 October 2026

Selected startups are introduced to:

  • The Brainforest team
  • Fellow cohort members
  • Program expectations
  • Resources and support systems

4. Venture Program

5 October – 11 December 2026

Founders participate in:

  • Weekly coaching
  • Strategy sessions
  • Business development workshops
  • Mentorship meetings
  • Investment readiness preparation
  • Pitch development

5. Community and Pitch Week

December 2026

The accelerator concludes with a Pitch Event in Zürich, where participants showcase their ventures before:

  • Investors
  • Partners
  • Industry experts
  • Brainforest community members

Graduating startups continue to benefit from the Brainforest network even after completing the program.

Program Impact

The Brainforest Venture Program has already built an impressive track record:

  • More than 1,000 applications received.
  • Over 50 founders have participated.
  • Nine portfolio companies supported.
  • More than 70% of participating founders are women.
  • Net Promoter Score (NPS) exceeding 80.

These achievements demonstrate the program’s commitment to supporting diverse founders while helping startups grow into successful impact-driven businesses.

Why Founders Should Apply

Successful applicants will benefit from:

  • Ten weeks of intensive venture acceleration.
  • Personalized one-on-one coaching.
  • Guidance from experienced mentors.
  • Access to biodiversity and conservation experts.
  • Networking with global impact investors.
  • Opportunity to receive a $125,000 equity investment.
  • Improved business strategy and investment readiness.
  • Stronger fundraising capabilities.
  • Lifetime access to the Brainforest community.
  • Opportunity to pitch before investors in Zürich.

How to Apply

Interested founders should prepare the latest version of their:

  • Pitch deck
  • Business documentation
  • Company information

Applicants must complete the online application before the deadline.

click HERE to apply

To learn more click HERE

Application Deadline: 17 August 2026

Conclusion

The Brainforest Venture Program 2026 offers one of the most specialized opportunities available for entrepreneurs building businesses that protect biodiversity while creating sustainable commercial value. Beyond funding, participants receive intensive coaching, expert mentorship, strategic guidance, and access to an international network of investors and conservation leaders. For startups committed to creating measurable environmental impact alongside financial growth, this accelerator provides an exceptional platform to strengthen their business, attract investment, and expand their global reach.

Founders developing innovative biodiversity-focused solutions are encouraged to submit their applications before 17 August 2026 to maximize their opportunity to join this highly competitive global program.

For more GLOBAL TRAINING click HERE

item.content:encoded:
Applications are open for the Pinterest Inclusion Fund 2026, a global incubator and creator development programme established to help emerging content creators build a stronger presence on Pinterest.

Now entering its sixth year, the programme will provide selected creators with financial support, personalised education, direct access to Pinterest and industry experts, content strategy training, collaboration opportunities and practical guidance on growing an audience through organic Pinterest content.

The 2026 Pinterest Inclusion Fund is particularly relevant to creators who are already producing content on other social media platforms but are new to Pinterest or have not yet developed a strong content strategy for the platform. It also encourages creators whose work supports Pinterest’s inclusive product features, including skin tone ranges, hair pattern search and body type ranges. icants using the Canadian application route, applications must be submitted by:

4 August 2026 at 9:00 p.m. Eastern Time

The application period opened on 21 July 2026 at 9:00 a.m. Eastern Time. the Pinterest Inclusion Fund

The Pinterest Inclusion Fund is an incubator and development pipeline designed to help emerging creators establish and expand their presence on Pinterest.

The programme combines direct financial assistance with training, education, community support and access to industry expertise. Instead of operating only as a one-time financial award, it aims to help participants understand how Pinterest works as a visual discovery platform and how creators can develop content that remains searchable, useful and discoverable over time.

Pinterest describes the programme as an opportunity for creators who are already active elsewhere online but are ready to build their Pinterest audience and improve their organic content strategy. Selected participants will receive personalised learning support, dedicated sessions with Pinterest and industry experts, and financial support to help fund content production. ramme also creates a pathway into Pinterest’s wider creator ecosystem. Participants who demonstrate strong engagement, consistent participation and meaningful growth during the programme may be invited to join the Pinterest Creator Community after completing the programme. Is New in the 2026 Pinterest Inclusion Fund?

The 2026 cycle marks the sixth year of the Pinterest Inclusion Fund.

This year, Pinterest is placing renewed emphasis on emerging creators who are already active on other platforms but are new to Pinterest or still developing their presence on the platform.

The programme is intended to unlock three main areas of support:

  1. Educational resources
  2. Financial support for content creation
  3. Growth opportunities within the Pinterest creator ecosystem

Pinterest is also broadening the range of content areas represented in the programme. While fashion, beauty and lifestyle remain central categories, the 2026 programme highlights creators producing content in areas such as:

  • Home and interior inspiration
  • Travel
  • Gaming
  • Technology
  • Health and wellness
  • Food
  • Fashion
  • Beauty
  • Lifestyle

The exact eligible content areas may differ slightly between national application pages. Candidates should therefore follow the criteria displayed on the application page for their country of legal residence. Objectives of the Programme

The Pinterest Inclusion Fund has been developed to help emerging creators overcome common barriers to building an audience on a new platform.

Its major objectives include:

  • Helping creators understand Pinterest’s content ecosystem
  • Increasing the visibility of diverse and inclusive content
  • Teaching creators how to develop a sustainable organic Pinterest strategy
  • Supporting the production of high-quality and inspirational content
  • Connecting emerging creators with experienced Pinterest and industry professionals
  • Helping creators understand platform trends and audience behaviour
  • Building a community of creators who can collaborate and learn from one another
  • Creating longer-term opportunities within the Pinterest Creator Community
  • Improving representation across Pinterest content categories
  • Helping new-to-Pinterest creators convert their existing creative experience into a platform-specific growth strategy

The programme is not simply intended for creators who already have large Pinterest audiences. It is particularly focused on creators who are ready to establish or significantly develop their presence on Pinterest.

Financial Support for Selected Creators

Selected participants will receive financial support intended to help fund the development and production of Pinterest content.

Pinterest’s current programme pages describe this support as financial assistance, grants or monetary incentives that participants can use to support their content creation activities. Pinterest has not publicly specified the exact amount of financial support available to each participant on the current application and programme pages.

Applicants should therefore avoid assuming that every participant will receive the same amount. The final value, payment method, eligible uses and applicable conditions are expected to be explained in the separate participant terms issued to successful applicants.

Submission of an application does not guarantee selection or financial support. Selected candidates must review and agree to the programme’s participant terms before joining. its of the Pinterest Inclusion Fund 2026

Selected creators may receive a combination of financial, educational and professional development support.

1. Financial Assistance for Content Creation

Participants will receive financial support to help them produce and optimise content for Pinterest.

This may help cover expenses associated with:

  • Content planning
  • Photography
  • Video production
  • Editing
  • Graphic design
  • Equipment
  • Props and materials
  • Styling
  • Research
  • Other content production requirements

The exact amount and permitted expenses have not been disclosed on the public programme pages.

2. Personalised Education

Participants will receive personalised educational support designed to reflect their experience, content category and growth objectives.

This is important because a content strategy that performs successfully on Instagram, TikTok, Facebook or YouTube may not automatically perform in the same way on Pinterest.

3. Direct Access to Pinterest Experts

Selected creators will receive dedicated learning time with Pinterest experts.

These sessions are expected to help participants understand:

  • How content is discovered on Pinterest
  • How users search for and save ideas
  • How to create useful and actionable Pins
  • How to structure boards
  • How to improve content discoverability
  • How to use Pinterest features effectively
  • How to develop a long-term organic growth strategy

4. Access to Industry Experts

The programme will also provide participants with learning opportunities involving professionals and experts from the wider content and creator industries.

This may allow participants to gain knowledge beyond the technical use of Pinterest, including insights into branding, creative planning, content production, audience development and professional growth.

5. Platform Best-Practice Training

Programme sessions will cover platform best practices that can help creators develop and grow their Pinterest presence.

Training topics may include:

  • Pinterest profile development
  • Board organisation
  • Pin optimisation
  • Organic content strategy
  • Audience growth
  • Search-based content discovery
  • Content consistency
  • Platform tools and features
  • Using Pinterest to expand the lifespan of existing content

6. Pinterest Trends and Insights

Participants will learn how to use Pinterest trends, insights and platform data to make better content decisions.

This may help creators identify:

  • Emerging content trends
  • Seasonal opportunities
  • Popular search topics
  • Audience interests
  • Content gaps
  • Opportunities for inclusive content
  • Subjects with longer-term discovery potential

7. Analytics Training

The programme will include deeper learning on content insights and analytics.

Participants may learn how to evaluate:

  • Pin impressions
  • Saves
  • Engagement
  • Outbound clicks
  • Audience interaction
  • Profile growth
  • Content performance
  • Long-term discovery patterns

Understanding these indicators can help creators identify what is working and improve their future content decisions.

8. Collaboration Sessions

The programme will offer dedicated collaboration sessions through which participants can connect with other emerging creators.

This creates opportunities to:

  • Share ideas
  • Discuss content challenges
  • Exchange practical strategies
  • Learn from creators in different content categories
  • Develop professional relationships
  • Identify possible collaborations

9. Office Hours

Selected participants will have access to office hours where they can receive more focused support, raise questions and obtain guidance on programme activities or Pinterest content development.

10. Potential Access to the Pinterest Creator Community

Creators who demonstrate meaningful engagement and growth throughout the programme may be invited to join the Pinterest Creator Community after graduation.

Pinterest states that this community may provide access to:

  • Monthly trends
  • Creator insights
  • Exclusive content challenges
  • Additional resources
  • Community opportunities
  • Early access to selected information or initiatives

An invitation is not automatic and will depend on the creator’s engagement and performance during the programme. reators Should Consider Applying

Pinterest operates differently from many conventional social media platforms.

Users often visit the platform to search for ideas, plan future activities, explore products and save useful content. This gives creators an opportunity to produce content that may continue to be discovered after its initial publication.

Pinterest reports that people who used its inclusive features saved 75% more Pins than users who did not use those features. Pinterest presents this as evidence that more inclusive content and search tools can create meaningful engagement and discovery opportunities. ation may therefore be valuable for creators seeking to:

  • Build a presence on Pinterest from the beginning
  • Diversify beyond Instagram, TikTok or YouTube
  • Increase the discoverability of existing content
  • Develop searchable and evergreen content
  • Strengthen their visual brand
  • Reach audiences looking for practical ideas
  • Build a more structured content strategy
  • Learn directly from platform experts
  • Receive assistance with content production
  • Become part of a professional creator community

Track Record of the Pinterest Inclusion Fund

The Pinterest Inclusion Fund was launched in 2021.

According to Pinterest, the programme has supported more than 500 content producers since its launch. Participants have received educational and financial support intended to help them develop their content, improve their understanding of Pinterest and create longer-term opportunities on the platform. t states that previous participants have experienced increased saves and engagement after joining the programme. These results are presented as evidence that structured training, platform knowledge and more consistent content production can help creators build stronger connections with Pinterest audiences. programme formats have supported creators, publishers, merchants and other content producers. The 2026 cycle, however, has returned to a creator-focused cohort. an Apply Through the Canadian Application?

The Canadian application form is open to creators who are legal residents of Canada and meet the programme’s eligibility conditions.

Applicants must meet the following requirements:

1. Creator or Content Producer

The applicant must identify as a creator or content producer.

The programme does not specify that content creation must be the applicant’s full-time occupation. However, the applicant must be actively creating and sharing content online.

2. Relevant Content Area

Applicants must create content within fashion, beauty or lifestyle-related areas.

The broader Canadian programme page also refers to associated areas including:

  • Home
  • Travel
  • Gaming
  • Technology
  • Health and wellness
  • Food

Candidates should clearly explain how their work falls within the relevant programme categories and how it could be adapted for Pinterest. ontent Supporting Inclusive Product Tools

The Canadian application page states that applicants must create fashion, beauty or lifestyle content that supports Pinterest’s inclusive product tools, particularly tools involving skin tone ranges or body type ranges. ts should therefore consider how their content:

  • Represents different skin tones
  • Reflects different body types
  • Improves representation
  • Provides useful ideas to wider audiences
  • Supports inclusive beauty or fashion discovery
  • Avoids narrow or exclusionary standards
  • Helps people find content relevant to their identities or needs

4. Legal Residency in Canada

Applicants using the Canadian form must be legal residents of Canada.

Citizenship is not expressly listed as a requirement on the application page. The stated condition is legal residency in Canada.

Applicants must be at least 18 years old at the time of application. Active on at Least Two Other Social Media Platforms

Applicants must be active and sharing content on at least two other social media platforms.

These platforms may include:

  • Instagram
  • TikTok
  • Facebook
  • YouTube
  • LinkedIn
  • Other recognised content platforms

The purpose of this condition is to identify applicants who are already actively producing content and are now ready to transfer or expand their creative strategy to Pinterest. nterest in Developing a Pinterest Strategy

Applicants must be interested in building an organic content strategy for Pinterest.

A successful application should therefore explain why Pinterest is relevant to the applicant’s content and what the creator wants to accomplish through the programme.

8. Availability for Programme Sessions

Applicants must be able to attend programme sessions and office hours.

Candidates should apply only if they can make a genuine commitment to:

  • Attend scheduled virtual sessions
  • Participate in office hours
  • Complete onboarding requirements
  • Produce Pinterest content
  • Apply programme guidance
  • Participate in required promotional activities
  • Remain actively engaged throughout the programme

What Information Is Requested in the Canadian Application?

The first part of the official Canadian application asks applicants to provide information including:

  • Email address
  • First name
  • Last name
  • Confirmation of legal residency in Canada
  • Confirmation that the applicant is at least 18 years old
  • Preferred pronouns, where the applicant wishes to provide them
  • Website address, where applicable
  • Whether the applicant has a Pinterest business account
  • Pinterest profile link
  • Pinterest username or handle
  • Instagram profile link
  • TikTok profile link
  • Facebook profile link, where applicable
  • LinkedIn profile link, where applicable

The form indicates that applicants without an applicable Pinterest profile or handle may enter “N/A” where instructed. Applicants should nevertheless consider establishing a professional Pinterest profile before applying because the purpose of the programme is to support creators seeking to grow on the platform. Will Selected Participants Be Required to Do?

Selection comes with active participation requirements.

Successful applicants will be expected to:

  1. Review and agree to separate programme participant terms
  2. Complete the programme’s onboarding requirements
  3. Attend virtual programme sessions
  4. Participate in office hours
  5. Create organic content for Pinterest
  6. Optimise content during the programme
  7. Apply Pinterest content best practices
  8. Use relevant platform features
  9. Participate in required promotional activities
  10. Remain engaged with the programme

Pinterest specifically refers to platform features such as:

  • Auto-import
  • Collages
  • Board sharing
  • Other Pinterest creation and content organisation tools

Participants should therefore be prepared to experiment with platform features rather than simply reposting their existing social media content without adaptation. cation and Selection Considerations

Pinterest states clearly that submitting an application does not guarantee selection.

Eligible applicants will still need to demonstrate that they are a strong fit for the programme. Although the full selection methodology is not publicly detailed, applicants are likely to be assessed on information such as:

  • Content quality
  • Relevance to the eligible content categories
  • Existing activity on other platforms
  • Potential to grow on Pinterest
  • Commitment to the programme
  • Alignment with inclusive content tools
  • Clarity of objectives
  • Ability to create useful, original and inspirational content

Applicants should provide accurate information and ensure that all submitted profile links are active, publicly accessible and representative of their strongest work.

Successful applicants will also be required to accept separate participant terms before formally joining the programme. o Prepare a Strong Application

Applicants should not treat the application as a routine social media registration form. They should present a clear case for why they are ready to build a meaningful presence on Pinterest.

1. Review Your Existing Social Profiles

Before applying, review your Instagram, TikTok, Facebook, YouTube or other relevant profiles.

Remove or archive content that does not reflect your current creative direction, and ensure your strongest work is easy to identify.

2. Clarify Your Content Category

Applicants should be able to describe their content in a focused way.

Instead of stating only that they are a “lifestyle creator,” they should identify a more specific direction, such as:

  • Inclusive fashion styling
  • Beauty content for different skin tones
  • Plus-size fashion inspiration
  • Accessible home organisation
  • Inclusive travel planning
  • Technology tutorials
  • Gaming lifestyle content
  • Wellness routines
  • Food and recipe content
  • Affordable interior design
  • Hair care for different hair patterns

3. Explain Why Pinterest Is Relevant

Applicants should explain why Pinterest is suitable for their content.

A strong explanation might focus on:

  • Visual discovery
  • Searchable content
  • Evergreen ideas
  • Audience planning behaviour
  • Product or website discovery
  • Long-term traffic
  • Content organisation through boards
  • Reaching audiences beyond existing platforms

4. Demonstrate Consistency

Pinterest is looking for active creators. Applicants should demonstrate that they publish content consistently and can commit to creating content during the programme.

5. Highlight Inclusive Content

Applicants should show how their content represents wider audiences or contributes to more inclusive visual discovery.

This is particularly important for Canadian applicants because the official application criteria specifically refer to Pinterest’s inclusive tools for skin tone and body type ranges.

6. Prepare Your Pinterest Account

Applicants should consider creating or improving their Pinterest profile before submitting the application.

Useful preparatory steps include:

  • Using a clear profile image
  • Writing a professional profile description
  • Adding a website link
  • Creating relevant boards
  • Publishing several high-quality Pins
  • Using clear Pin titles and descriptions
  • Organising content by category
  • Ensuring the profile reflects the applicant’s content niche

7. Verify Every Link

All profile and website links should be checked before submission.

Broken, private or incorrect profile links could prevent reviewers from evaluating the applicant’s work properly.

8. Apply Before the Final Hours

Applicants should submit their forms well before the deadline.

Waiting until the final hours creates unnecessary risks, including internet problems, incomplete submissions or technical issues with the form.

Click HERE to apply for Canada based.
Click HERE to apply for US based.

Important Deadline

For the Canada-based creator application cycle, the application period is:

Opening date: 21 July 2026 at 9:00 a.m. Eastern Time

Application deadline: 4 August 2026 at 9:00 p.m. Eastern Time

Late applications may not be accepted. Candidates should complete the official application form and verify that their submission has been successfully recorded before the deadline. ts in Australia and New Zealand have the same calendar deadline of 4 August 2026, but the official local programme page specifies 9:00 p.m. Australian Eastern Standard Time. Applicants in other countries should verify the exact local deadline on the relevant country-specific page. tant Information Not Yet Publicly Disclosed

Pinterest’s public 2026 programme and application pages do not currently specify:

  • The exact amount of financial support per participant
  • The total number of creators who will be selected
  • The full programme duration
  • The programme start and completion dates
  • The complete selection scoring methodology
  • The date on which successful applicants will be notified
  • Whether unsuccessful applicants will receive individual feedback

Applicants should not rely on amounts, dates or programme arrangements from previous years because the structure may change between application cycles.

Successful candidates should carefully review the official participant terms before accepting an offer.

Conclusion

The Pinterest Inclusion Fund 2026 offers emerging content creators a valuable opportunity to develop a professional Pinterest strategy while receiving financial support, expert guidance, educational resources and access to a wider creator community.

The programme is especially suitable for creators who are already active on platforms such as Instagram, TikTok, Facebook or YouTube but have not yet established a strong presence on Pinterest. It is also relevant to creators producing inclusive, inspirational and practical content across fashion, beauty, lifestyle, home, travel, gaming, technology, wellness and food-related areas.

Canadian applicants must be legal residents of Canada, at least 18 years old, active on at least two other social platforms and available to attend programme sessions and office hours. Their content must also meet the requirements stated on the Canadian application page.

Eligible creators should prepare their social profiles, clarify their content niche, review their Pinterest strategy and submit the application before 4 August 2026 at 9:00 p.m. Eastern Time.
